functions.name: UpdateSuspensionAndWheelPhysics
functions.summary: Per-frame vehicle physics update: copies and adjusts the four wheel contact-patch positions, recomputes weight distribution from the car-setup block (a2), rebuilds per-wheel suspension/tire state (temperatures, loads, spring/damper split), computes anti-roll bar mixing and drivetrain/mass parameters, runs a 13-point contact-position transform (with per-point bitmask-driven tweaks and a bounding-radius tracking), evaluates six polynomial/tire-force helper models, sums the resulting force vector, applies session (a3) offsets to the tracked contact points, fills a 13-point particle buffer, writes the wheel output positions, and returns an advanced pointer into the session block. Reads configuration from a2 (car setup) and a3 (session/track state); writes results back into the vehicle struct (this).

Loop 4 times over the car-setup block (a2, stride 704 bytes), accumulating each spring-rate contribution (integer * setup double + setup double) into this+0x4024.
Compute the front/rear suspension reference offsets v201, v202, v203 and v264 from session values a3+96/112/120/128 and the axle-average fields this+0x3594/0x368C/0x377C/0x387C.

If the physics-mode flag this+0x32BC is zero, override v201/v202/v203 from the current body-offset fields this+0x72C/0x730/0x734 minus the global constants dbl_7C8A24 / dbl_7C8A2C / dbl_7C8A34 (fallback body position).

functions.name: SetWheelForceParameters
functions.summary: Conditional wheel force/torque parameter setter. If enable flag this+0x32BC is non-zero, stores the four float parameters a2..a5 into wheel-force struct fields (this+0x3664, +0x375C, +0x3854, +0x394C). Otherwise bypasses storage and directly applies a2..a5 as force/torque to a rigid body via ForceTorqueApplicationToRigidBodyWithInertiaTens, passing the dbl_7C7428 scalar as the inertia-tensor argument. Called from PitStopProgress during pit-stop wheel operations.

Store parameter a2 into wheel-force field this+0x3664.
Store parameter a3 into wheel-force field this+0x375C.
Store parameter a4 into wheel-force field this+0x3854.
Store parameter a5 into wheel-force field this+0x394C.
Direct-apply path: call ForceTorqueApplicationToRigidBodyWithInertiaTens with global dbl_7C7428 and parameters a2..a5.

The four fields at +0x3664/+0x375C/+0x3854/+0x394C are recalculated every frame elsewhere, so stored values are transient (persistence verdict: recalced).
Callee identity of the helper is provided only by name in existing analysis; no callee address evidence is in the packet.

functions.name: ParseSvmHdvVehicleConfigFile
functions.summary: Line-by-line parser for .SVM/.HDV vehicle configuration files. Opens the file in binary-read mode, runs an optional first-pass format check that rejects files with no recognized section header, then iterates lines and dispatches each section (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, per-wheel corners, Basic) to a section-specific reader. Token readers (int/float/string/bool) populate the internal vehicle setup struct (this) and normalize range/setting pairs into the output vehicle state struct (a3); several sections resolve and parse secondary files (damage model, engine, gear file) relative to the config path. Ends with track-config finalization and stream cleanup.

operations.description: Open the config file in binary-read mode ("rb") via sub_534B00; if the handle is null, free the pending path buffer with FreeWrapper_7bcf and return -1.

First-pass format validation (a4 bit 0): scan for the '=' delimiter (sub_589DB0) and require at least one recognized section header among Setting/Notes/Downforce/Balance/Ride/Gearing/Custom/Symmetric (sub_587C20). If none found and this is not a server session (dword_7C569C != 5), write the "%s is an illegal .SVM file" message via StringSplitLoop/DebugLogWrite into dword_8AD25C, then rewind the stream with AudioStreamBufferRead, close it via StreamFileTypeCheckWithDispatch, free the path buffer and abort.

Main parse loop: read the next line with LineInputReader, decode its token type with sub_5651B0 (0=data line, 1=end-of-section, else stop), then match the section header with sub_587C20 and dispatch to the matching section parser.

General section: read scalar/vector settings (Rules, GarageDisplayFlags, FeelerFlags, Mass, Inertia, CgHeight, WedgePushrod, GraphicalOffsets, the four Undertrays, FuelTankPos/Motion, AI aid/performance scalars, Notes, Symmetric) with the int/float/string token readers into this-relative fields; mirror selected values into the output struct (a3+6544 Rules, a3+6540 garage-display, a3+6556 wedge-pushrod, a3+6565 symmetric). Rules also lands at this+0x34, garage-display at this+0x38, wedge-pushrod copied from this+0x68; Notes goes through sub_5665B0.

General section, tire brand: parse TireBrand, strip the filename extension, copy the brand into the output vehicle name via NameStringCopy, then look it up with TireBrandLookup(&dword_8AD254); on success copy the compound's data into the output struct and write the this+0x8 tire-compound RPM multiplier; on an unknown brand, in non-server sessions, emit "*.hdv file references unknown tire compound" via StringSplitLoop/DebugLogWrite. Missing compound path falls back to byte_5EA438 before StringCopyWithBufferRealloc.

General section, damage file: when DamageFile is present, resolve the .ini with FileFinder against the config path; when the a4 bit-2 parse flag is clear, parse it with VehicleDamageModel into this+6128; store the resolved path (fallback byte_5EA438) via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc.
General section: normalize range/setting pairs into the output struct via CRTMathHelper_e1f0 for CgRight, CgRear, Wedge, TireCompound, Fuel, NumPitStops and PitStop1/PitStop2/PitStop3.
